hints: Identify forces parallel to the smooth plane: pulling force $200\text{ N}$ up, weight component $mg\sin 20^\circ$ down.
Apply Newton's second law: $F_{\text{net}} = 200 - mg\sin 20^\circ = ma$.
Solve for $a$ with $m = 30\text{ kg}$ and $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$.
walkthrough:
Step 1: Identify forces acting on the particle parallel to the smooth inclined plane:
- Constant pulling force directed up the plane: $P = 200\text{ N}$.
- Downward component of weight acting down the incline: $W_{\text{parallel}} = mg\sin 20^\circ = 30(10)\sin 20^\circ = 300\sin 20^\circ\text{ N}$.
- Since the plane is smooth, there is no friction.

Step 2: Apply Newton's second law along the plane in the upward direction:
$$F_{\text{net}} = ma$$
$$200 - 300\sin 20^\circ = 30a$$
$$200 - 300(0.342020) = 30a$$
$$200 - 102.606 = 30a$$
$$97.394 = 30a$$
$$a = \frac{97.394}{30} \approx 3.2465\text{ m s}^{-2} \approx 3.25\text{ m s}^{-2}$$
The acceleration of the particle is $3.25\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

hints: Recall the work-energy theorem: net work done by all forces equals change in kinetic energy ($\Delta E_k = F_{\text{net}} \times d$).
Alternatively, find $v^2 = u^2 + 2as$ over distance $12\text{ m}$ and compute $\frac{1}{2}mv^2$.
Multiply net force ($97.39\text{ N}$) by $12\text{ m}$.
walkthrough:
Step 1: State the work-energy theorem:
The change in kinetic energy equals the net work done on the particle by the resultant force parallel to the displacement:
$$\Delta E_k = F_{\text{net}} \times d$$

Step 2: Substitute the net force $F_{\text{net}} = 97.394\text{ N}$ and distance $d = 12\text{ m}$:
$$\Delta E_k = 97.394 \times 12 = 1168.73\text{ J} \approx 1170\text{ J}$$
Alternatively, using kinematics $v^2 = u^2 + 2as$ with $u = 0$:
$$v^2 = 2(3.24647)(12) = 77.915\text{ m}^2\text{ s}^{-2}$$
$$\Delta E_k = \frac{1}{2}mv^2 = \frac{1}{2}(30)(77.915) = 1168.7\text{ J} \approx 1170\text{ J}$$
The increase in kinetic energy is $1170\text{ J}$.

hints: Resolve perpendicular to the rough plane to find normal reaction: $R = mg\cos 20^\circ = 300\cos 20^\circ$.
Apply Newton's second law parallel to slope: $200 - mg\sin 20^\circ - F = ma$, and solve for $a$.
walkthrough:
Step 1: Resolve forces perpendicular to the plane to find the normal reaction $R$:
Because there is no motion perpendicular to the plane:
$$R = mg\cos 20^\circ = 30(10)\cos 20^\circ = 300(0.939693) \approx 281.908\text{ N}$$

Step 2: Calculate the limiting frictional force opposing upward motion using $\mu = 0.12$:
$$F = \mu R = 0.12 \times 281.908 \approx 33.829\text{ N}$$

Step 3: Apply Newton's second law parallel to the plane up the slope:
$$F_{\text{net}} = ma$$
$$200 - mg\sin 20^\circ - F = 30a$$
$$200 - 300\sin 20^\circ - 33.829 = 30a$$
$$200 - 102.606 - 33.829 = 30a$$
$$63.565 = 30a$$
$$a = \frac{63.565}{30} \approx 2.1188\text{ m s}^{-2} \approx 2.12\text{ m s}^{-2}$$
The acceleration of the particle is $2.12\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

hints: The 200 N force acts at $10^\circ$ to the plane. Its components are $200\cos 10^\circ$ parallel and $200\sin 10^\circ$ perpendicular (pulling upward).
Calculate new friction $F = \mu R$, then apply Newton's second law: $200\cos 10^\circ - mg\sin 20^\circ - F = ma$.
walkthrough:
Step 1: Resolve forces perpendicular to the incline when the pulling force acts at $10^\circ$ above the plane:
The pulling force now has an upward component perpendicular to the slope ($200\sin 10^\circ$):
$$R + 200\sin 10^\circ = mg\cos 20^\circ$$
$$R = 300\cos 20^\circ - 200\sin 10^\circ$$
$$R = 281.908 - 200(0.173648) = 281.908 - 34.730 = 247.178\text{ N}$$

Step 2: Calculate the revised frictional force using $\mu = 0.12$:
$$F = \mu R = 0.12 \times 247.178 \approx 29.661\text{ N}$$

Step 3: Apply Newton's second law parallel to the plane up the slope:
The component of the pulling force parallel to the slope is $200\cos 10^\circ$:
$$F_{\text{net}} = ma$$
$$200\cos 10^\circ - mg\sin 20^\circ - F = 30a$$
$$200(0.984808) - 102.606 - 29.661 = 30a$$
$$196.962 - 132.267 = 30a$$
$$64.695 = 30a$$
$$a = \frac{64.695}{30} \approx 2.1565\text{ m s}^{-2} \approx 2.16\text{ m s}^{-2}$$
The acceleration of the particle is $2.16\text{ m s}^{-2}$.
